Reframing the September 22, 2021 FOMC statement with insights from monetary economics: The tone is cautiously positive. The Committee reaffirms average inflation targeting (Powell’s 2020 shift to a make‑up strategy) and uses forward guidance and QE to manage expectations—consistent with the Woodford/Svensson view that expectations are the transmission channel and that temporary supply shocks should largely be “looked through” while keeping long‑run inflation expectations anchored at 2 percent. Maintaining the policy rate at the zero lower bound and operating the floor system with interest on reserves, ON RRP, and repo facilities aligns with the post‑2008 framework and Bernanke‑style toolkit (QE, forward guidance) to provide accommodation when conventional policy is constrained. At the same time, the explicit signal that “a moderation in the pace of asset purchases may soon be warranted” is a mild hawkish tilt, consistent with the Clarida/Taylor‑principle perspective that policy should normalize as inflation and employment goals come into view; via the signaling channel, such taper talk can lift longer‑term yields (Cochrane–Piazzesi), tempering risk appetite. Balancing these elements, the communication is supportive of growth and employment but tempered by taper guidance and COVID‑related risks—moderately positive rather than strongly dovish.
